name: Pengo
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Burrow, T. & S. Bhattacharya 1970. The Pengo Language: Grammar, Texts and Vocabulary. Oxford: Clarendon (not online).

sources.citation: Nagamma Reddy, K. [2003]. Phonetic characteristics of phonemic systems of Indian languages (segmentals). International Journal of Dravidian Linguistics XXXII(2): c. 30-55.
sources.note: Pengo appears only in a list of languages by nasal-consonant inventory. Generic remark that in Dravidian 'the stress is not contrastive and all are intonational languages'; suprasegmentals explicitly reserved 'for future study'. No Pengo-specific stress statement.

sources.citation: Starostin, G. S. 2016. Annotated Swadesh wordlists for the Gondi-Kui group (Konda, Pengo, Manda, Kui, Kuwi): data sources and transliteration notes. Global Lexicostatistical Database.
sources.note: Transliteration notes for Pengo (retroflex recoding, long vowels, c/j as palatal affricates); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Ramakrishna Reddy, B. 2009. Number system in Manda: interplay of phonology, morphosyntax and semantics. International Journal of Dravidian Linguistics XXXVIII(1): 19ff. (in archive.org item for IJDL vol. XXXIX).
sources.note: About Manda (sister language); mentions Pengo only for classification/ethnonym (awut). Nothing on Pengo stress.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Pengo language' (phoneme tables cited to Krishnamurti 2003:56).
sources.note: Vowel and consonant tables only; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Ramakrishna Reddy, B. [2001]. Survey of research on Central and South-Central Dravidian tribal languages (section 'The Kondh languages'). International Journal of Dravidian Linguistics XXX(2): c. 120-135.
sources.note: Bibliographic survey: Pengo grammar = Burrow & Bhattacharya 1970 ('section on phonology deals with the synchronic status and the diachronic development of Pengo sounds'); Avut dialect of Pengo described in Subba Rao 1982 Osmania M.Phil.; Indi-Awe in Ramanaiah 1982 Osmania M.Phil. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Marr, J. R. 1971. Review of T. Burrow & S. Bhattacharya, The Pengo language. Bulletin of the School of Oriental and African Studies 34: 672.
sources.note: Short notice describing the book's layout (grammar pp. 3-107, texts, vocabulary) and the verb system; nothing on accent or stress.

sources.citation: Andronov, M. S. 1970. Dravidian Languages (transl. D. M. Segal). Moscow: Nauka.
sources.note: Names Pengo only as one of the 'still unknown languages'; no data on it.

sources.citation: PHOIBLE 2.0 inventory 1779 Pengo (source RA = Ramaswami 1999, Common Linguistic Features in Indian Languages: Phonetics, CIIL, based on Burrow & Bhattacharya 1970).
sources.note: Segment inventory only; no stress/tone information.

sources.citation: Andronov, M. S. 2003. A Comparative Grammar of the Dravidian Languages. München: LINCOM (English ed. of Sravnitel'naja grammatika dravidijskix jazykov, 1978), section on accent/stress.

sources.note: Andronov's comparative grammar surveys word accent language by language from the published grammars; would show whether anything is on record for Pengo (second-hand).

sources.citation: Krishnamurti, Bh. 2003. The Dravidian Languages. Cambridge: CUP, ch. 2 (descriptive phonology; Pengo inventory p. 56ff.)
